newsitem.title: USA: Shell, Texaco, Saudis finalize U.S refining deal.
newsitem.headline: Shell, Texaco, Saudis finalize U.S refining deal.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Oil Co., Texaco Inc. and Saudi Aramco said they had reached a final agreement to combine their U.S. Eastern and Gulf Coast refining and marketing operations.

The new venture will be 35 percent owned by Shell, 32.5 percent by Texaco and 32.5 percent by Saudi Aramco's Saudi Refining Inc. unit. Saudi Aramco is the government-owned oil company of Saudi Arabia.
The completion of the deal follows the merger earlier this year of Shell and Texaco's refining and marketing units on the West Coast.
The new company will continue to market gasoline under both the Texaco and Shell brands, the companies said.

"We believe this combination of the three companies' assets will allow us to accomplish fundamental change in the way we operate our downstream businesses, leading to improved performance and growth," the three company chief executives said in a statement.
The three-company venture will have a refining capacity of 823,000 barrels per day and 14,717 retail outlets.
Shell and Texaco will separately operate 11,212 retail outlets and 948,000 barrels per day of refining capacity as part of their West Coast alliance.
The companies said they anticipated significant savings from the venture and "that these savings are not based upon closure of refiners or other major operating facilities".
They expect to form the new company next year, once regulatory and other approvals are obtained.
